rv.q: Let me make an unsolicited suggestion to triple the Lookingglass Theatre box office. Instead of calling the current show "Untitled Vampire Play," which is bloodless to the point of vegetarianism, make it "Hey, Mom and Dad, My Fiancée is a Vampire!" Ka-ching on the Magnificent Mile.
This play—easily one of the best of the year—has everything.
Every scene hits exactly as intended. Every performance is perfectly calibrated. And every joke and emotional moment lands. That's a rare, rare feat.
With heart, fun, and a touch of horror, The Untitled Vampire Play is an event that you will not want to miss.
By the poignant conclusion, we see something richer and more mournful at work that offers a metaphorical stake to our hearts.
Kevin Douglas' latest play, now having its world premiere at Lookingglass Theatre, is filled with Fangtastic Fun. There's something in this play for everyone.
The production is seamless and flows throughout its 2-hour-and-15-minute runtime.
While it doesn't entirely break new ground, Untitled Vampire Play is creative and visually arresting.
The new Untitled Vampire Play by Kevin Douglas is a fun night out, but be sure to wear something washable because there are literally buckets of blood.
I would say don't miss this powerful ending, and the fun inbetween.
For something quite different and entertaining in theater, I would highly recommend Untitled Vampire Play at Lookingglass Theater.
